title: Recognition of Sentences
theory:
Simple Sentence
  A sentence that contains only one independent clause (one finite verb).
 1. He works hard.
 2. To earn money, he started a business.

 Compound Sentence
  A sentence that contains two or more independent clauses joined by coordinating
 conjunctions ( FANBOYS= for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so).
 1. He worked hard, and he passed the exam.
 2. I wanted to go out, but it was raining.

 Complex Sentence
  A sentence that contains one independent clause and at least one dependent
 (subordinate) clause.

 Because, If, Although, Though, Even though, Even if, Unless, Until, When, While,
 Before, After, As, Since, Who, Whom, Which, What, That etc.
 1. When he arrived, the meeting had started.
 2. I know that she is honest.

 Compound-complex Sentence
  A sentence that has three or more clauses, including at least one main clause joined
 by a coordinating conjunction and one dependent clause joined by a subordinating
 conjunction.
